text.p: New York Times Co Chief Financial Officer Diane Baker said the company expects to post earnings of $1.78-$1.88, versus $1.41 in 1995.
Baker, speaking at a PaineWebber conference, said the 1996 estimates excludes one-time items such as acquisition, divestitures, accounting changes and worker buyouts.
Baker, said the company was recording a "strong fourth quarter" but did not elaborate.
Baker said the company expects advertising revenue to be up 4-6 percent in 1997 from 1996, and expects newsprint costs to decline 11 to 13 percent.
Baker said operating profit for its newpaper group is expected to increase $336-$346 million in 1996 excluding severance cost compared to $231 million in 1995.
Baker said capital spending for 1996 will totaled about $240 million compared to $212 million in 1995.
Free cash flow should range from 338-$348 million in 1996 versus $280 million in 1995.

Arthur Sulzberger Jr, publisher of the New York Times newspaper, reiterated a forecast that circulation of the national edition of paper was expected to rise to 500,000 within the next five years from about 400,000 currently.
